newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada union says deal closer with Chrysler.
newsitem.headline: Canada union says deal closer with Chrysler.

text.p: Chrysler Corp's Chrysler Canada took an important step closer to the Canadian Auto Workers union's position on outsourcing on Sunday, but the two sides still have a long way to go ahead of Tuesday's midnight strike deadline, CAW president Buzz Hargrove said during a break in bargaining.

Hargrove said Chrysler's latest proposal on outsourcing, presented to the union this afternoon, recognized the principle of work ownership, a key component of outsourcing, but did not limit the automaker's ability to contract out the work.

"We own the work; the next step has to be that we have some say in what happens to it," said Hargrove. "It does now recognize the principle, in writing, of work ownership; but you could drive a truck through the language after that, so we are still an awful long ways apart," Hargrove told reporters.

The union said work is owned by the union when workers are "producing quality products in a productive manner at reasonably low cost, and (the company is) making a reasonable profit." Hargrove said once the company recognizes work ownership, it follows that the company cannot contract out the work without replacing it with other jobs.
Chrysler could not be reached for comment.
Hargrove said he had not expected Chrysler to concede the work ownership issue before a strike, but the early move to do so is only the first step towards controlling outsourcing.
"If you're looking down that tunnel, you'll see a little small light, but boy, it is faint," said Hargrove.

He said the union will present a counterproposal on this issue later today but does not expect to hear back from the company on outsourcing until Monday. Hargrove said the union will not budge from its commitment to restrict outsourcing, and until the issue is settled the talks cannot move forward.

"We have a whole host of other issues that aren't moving because of this issue," said Hargrove. "It starts to get very dicey as to whether we can do this, even working around the clock, if we don't find a way to resolve this issue in the next few hours."
The union said its 12,600 Chrysler workers will strike the automaker if an agreement is not reached by 2359 EDT Tuesday/0359 GMT Wednesday.
A collective agreement with Chrysler will become the framework for negotiations between the union and the Canadian units of General Motors Corp and Ford Motor Co.
